refined_description: Entry step. Generate the benchmark input text of W=5000 total words. For the input text generation, use [cat, dog, bird, horse, pig], each distributed evenly and shuffled randomly (M=5 different words, 1000 occurrences each). Build a list with W/len(vocab) copies of each word, shuffle it with Python's random module, and write it as a single plain-text file of whitespace-separated words. W and the vocabulary should be overridable via function arguments with these defaults. This is the only vocabulary-specific step.

The split function partitions the input text into N batches (N=3, the number of mapping functions; configurable via a function argument). Read the full input text, tokenize on whitespace, and divide the word sequence into N contiguous, near-equal batches (sizes differ by at most one; no word is lost or duplicated). Write one plain-text batch per mapper, numbered 1..N to match the mapper ranks. Must work for any input text, vocabulary size and word frequency.

Ranked map step (N=3 instances). N parallel map functions count how often each word occurs in their text chunk: each instance uses faasr_rank() to read the text batch matching its rank, counts word occurrences with no hard-coded vocabulary (any words, any frequency), and writes its partial count dictionary Y_i (word -> count) as JSON, numbered by its rank. Must be fully generalizable to vocabularies of any size and frequency.

Shuffle flattens the resulting array Y_i of per-mapper word counts. The available workflow primitives necessitate the shuffle function, not relying on the array Y_i itself but flattening it to enable the desired level of parallelism in reduce. Read all N mapper partial-count files (N configurable via argument), flatten them into a list of (word, partial_count) pairs grouped by word, sort the distinct words deterministically, and partition them across the M reducers (M=5, configurable via argument) round-robin by sorted index so every word goes to exactly one reducer. Write one JSON partition per reducer rank 1..M mapping each assigned word to its list of partial counts; a reducer with no words gets an empty object. Must be fully generalizable to vocabularies of any size and frequency (number of distinct words may be smaller or larger than M).

Ranked reduce step (M=5 instances). M reducers count the total occurrences of their respective word(s) in parallel, yielding Z_i. Each instance uses faasr_rank() to read the shuffle partition matching its rank, sums the list of partial counts for each word in that partition, and writes Z_i (word -> total count) as JSON numbered by its rank. Handles an empty partition (writes an empty object). Must be fully generalizable to vocabularies of any size and frequency.
